questions.q: Why does ordinary KFold cross-validation leak future information when applied to time series data?
options: Because it always uses shuffle=True by default
Because every fold takes a turn as the test set, so for most folds the training set includes data from after the test period in time
Because KFold cannot handle more than 5 splits
Because KFold requires labeled anomaly data
questions.explain: K-fold rotates which fold is held out as test. For every fold except possibly the very first, the remaining training folds include observations from after the test period — a leak that exists regardless of the shuffle setting.

questions.q: What does sklearn's TimeSeriesSplit guarantee about each train/test split?
options: That train and test sets are always the same size
That the training set always comes strictly before the test set in time
That the data is shuffled before splitting
That labels are purged of any overlap
questions.explain: TimeSeriesSplit produces successive splits where every test fold comes strictly after its corresponding training fold in calendar time, never before and never overlapping.

questions.q: What is the difference between TimeSeriesSplit's default behavior and setting max_train_size?
options: The default is a rolling window; max_train_size switches to an expanding window
The default is an expanding window that keeps growing; max_train_size caps training to a fixed-size rolling window
max_train_size disables time ordering entirely
There is no difference; max_train_size only affects test set size
questions.explain: By default TimeSeriesSplit uses an expanding window where each training set is a superset of the previous one. Passing max_train_size caps the window to a fixed size, creating a rolling window that drops old data as it advances.

questions.q: According to the lesson, why is TimeSeriesSplit's time-ordering guarantee not sufficient on its own for many financial ML problems?
options: Because TimeSeriesSplit is deprecated in current scikit-learn versions
Because financial labels are often built from windows that extend into the future beyond a row's own timestamp, creating overlap even when train precedes test
Because TimeSeriesSplit only works on classification problems
Because it requires GPU acceleration to run
questions.explain: A label like 'return over the next 5 days' depends on information past its own row's timestamp. Even when training rows come before the test period in time, their labels can overlap into the test window, which TimeSeriesSplit's ordering guarantee alone doesn't prevent.

questions.q: What does the gap parameter in TimeSeriesSplit do?
options: It removes a buffer of samples between the end of training and the start of test
It increases the number of cross-validation folds
It shuffles the gap between folds randomly
It is only used for classification labels, not regression
questions.explain: The gap parameter inserts a buffer of excluded samples between the training set and the test set, a concept that becomes directly relevant for purging and embargoing in the next lesson.
